purpose: Evaluate nuisance-adjusted common-SNP association tests for simulated continuous cardiometabolic and binary mental-health outcomes
author: Vusumuzi Mabasa
data_scope: Fully synthetic independent people and genotypes; no patient data, AWI-Gen or Genomic SEM
covariates: Age-like standard normal clipped at +/-2.5; exposure Bernoulli(0.5) minus 0.5; both included linearly in both fitted margins
continuous_margin: Mean 0.35*age + 0.25*exposure + beta1*(G0-2*maf); unit normal marginal residual
binary_margin: Probit predictor intercept + 0.25*age + 0.4*exposure + beta2*(G0-2*maf); intercept calibrated by independent population quadrature

dependence.t_varying: t copula with 4 df and varying latent correlation; transformed to normal residual margins

LD: Two independent haplotypes from thresholded latent Gaussian AR(1); 0.6 denotes latent-normal correlation, not diploid LD
primary_target: Focal SNP0 omnibus H0 beta1=beta2=0; not a test of pleiotropy, shared causality, causal disease direction or fine-mapping
score: Model-based observed efficient-information statistic and nuisance-adjusted sandwich score statistic; 2 df if information is positive and full rank
calibration: For each method and stratum, the 10th smallest p among 200 independent null datasets is frozen; reject strictly below this cutoff. This targets 10/201 under exchangeability over calibration banks, with conservative ties; conditional size can differ. Any calibration fit failure disables that arm's empirical cutoff.
nominal_testing: Report uncalibrated chi-square p rejection at 0.05 and 0.01; do not infer calibration at 5e-8
effect_intervals: Full alternative-model fits on the first prespecified replicate indices for every scenario, regardless of significance; model and sandwich Wald intervals are evaluated, not assumed valid
failure_policy: Never drop failed fits; publish statuses. Nominal rejection denominators include all attempted datasets with failures as non-rejections, alongside failure rates and valid-fit denominators. Empirical calibration is unavailable if any calibration fit fails.
Monte_Carlo: Within-stratum standard errors; paired method contrasts on identical datasets. Calibration-bank uncertainty is not included in conditional evaluation MCSEs.
limits: Small common-SNP panels, not an executed genome-wide scan
No background polygenic effects, population structure, relatedness, missingness or ascertainment in this first experiment
No real clinical or biological claims
No novelty claim for copula GWAS, score testing or covariate-dependent copula regression
No external LD reference is used
No CBMAT variant-set comparison: targets differ
ApproxCopula is contextual prior work, not an executed comparator
